title: Strong Correlation With Stock Losses
summary:
Strong Correlation With Stock Losses 

             
             
            Bonds continue hanging back and letting other markets set the tone. For the most part, that's entailed a focus weakness in the stock market. In response, there have been multiple episodes of small-scale flights to safety in the bond market. Coming into the this week, there was a question as to how strong that correlation would be in light of last week's inflation-driven breakdown. As it stands, stock prices and bond yields are still doing a good job of moving in the same direction at the same time, but the magnitude of the movement in bonds leaves something to be desired. Bottom line: bonds started weaker and were only able to turn green because stocks sold off aggressively enough.

title: Another Small Victory For Mortgage Rates
summary: The present week continues to be rather uneventful for mortgage rates, although not at all unpleasant. It began with Monday largely holding in line with Friday's latest levels. While those were the highest in several weeks, we've made slow and steady progress since then.   Each of the past 3 days has resulted in modest improvement with today's installment being the smallest so far at only 0.01%. The only caveat is that rates have needed some help in order to keep this gentle progress intact.  A vast majority of "help" since early-to-mid October has come in the form of a stock market correction and general concerns over the sustainability of the AI boom. This has resulted in bond yields frequently correlating with major stock market averages like the NASDAQ or S&P.   Today was no exception. Bonds were slightly weaker at first (thus implying slightly higher mortgage rates). It wasn't until stocks began to swoon around 10am ET that bond yields dropped, thus allowing mortgage lenders to set today's rates a bit lower than they otherwise could have.

title: Bonds Getting Some Help From Stocks
summary: It's been a boring and mostly sideways session for the bond market so far today. Initial overnight gains gave way to modest weakness in the overnight session. Both stocks and oil prices were moving slightly higher at the same time. The S&P has been selling in the 10am hour and that has spilled over into bond market improvement. In the bigger picture, however, bonds are basically flat so far and still consolidating in a broadly sideways pattern after last week's sell-off. If stocks were to convincingly break below yesterday's lows, we could see a stronger response in bonds.

title: Fed Minutes Show Mortgage Demand Weak Despite Easier Credit
summary: Minutes from the Federal Reserve's Oct. 27–28 meeting, released Wednesday, show that mortgage credit availability continued to improve gradually even as higher interest rates kept origination activity subdued.The Fed's staff reported that residential mortgage activity had declined further amid a sharp rise in mortgage rates. Policymakers also cited higher borrowing costs as a drag on residential investment, even as the broader economy continued to expand.The Fed's October Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey, released Nov. 2, offers a closer look at the disconnect.

title: Housing Market May Have Found Its Bottom. What Comes Next?
summary: The housing market may finally be approaching the bottom of its current downturn, but the bigger question is how long it could remain there.Pending home sales fell 4.7% in October to their lowest level since the National Association of Realtors (NAR) began tracking the data in 2001. Contract signings were down 16.7% from a year earlier, marking the second consecutive month of record-low activity.Yet NAR Chief Economist Lawrence Yun sees a possible turning point.

title: Newrez Agrees to $3 Million Settlement Over Servicing Violations
summary: Newrez has reached its second major mortgage servicing settlement in three months, agreeing to $3 million in payments and system improvements after Washington regulators investigated more than 125 consumer complaints involving loan servicing errors and alleged unfair or deceptive practices.

title: Pending Home Sales Fall 15.3% Despite Growing Buyer Leverage
summary: Pending home sales fell 15.3% year over year during the four weeks ending Nov. 15, declining in every major metropolitan area analyzed by Redfin. Nationally, pending sales slipped 0.3% from the previous week to 276,187, the lowest level in the brokerage's records dating back to 2021.The weakness comes despite four consecutive weeks of year-over-year home-price declines and a recent dip in monthly mortgage payments. With borrowing costs climbing again, lenders face the prospect of continued pressure on purchase volume heading into year-end.

title: NEXA Adds $100M VA Producer as Wholesale Recruiting Continues
summary: NEXA Lending has recruited another high-producing VA loan originator, adding Michael Lindsay to its national network as the wholesale brokerage continues attracting established producers from the retail channel.Lindsay, a military veteran who originated more than $100 million in mortgages in 2025, according to NEXA, joins the Phoenix-based company with approximately 98% to 99% of his production concentrated in VA loans. Licensed in roughly 35 states, he expects to close between $80 million and $85 million in 2026.
